policy.last_change: 4 Mar 2026 (-25bp, eff. 5 Mar); held 9 Apr, 6 May and 2 Jun

policy.pricing_text: FRAs at the 16 Jun close (1x4 3.84, 3x6 3.87, 6x9 3.93, 9x12 4.00 vs WIBOR 3M 3.85) price roughly 15bp of NBP hikes within 12 months. The MPC held at 3.75% on 2 Jun (May CPI eased mainly on food; decisions stay data-dependent); Glapiński (3 Jun): lower May CPI cuts the hike odds, rates are high enough and there is no reason to change or even discuss them. Kotecki (15 Jun): rate changes unlikely to end-2026, hike appetite lower, too early to signal cuts; Dąbrowski (12 Jun): a cut now more likely than a hike. May CPI 3.1% (final, 15 Jun; flash 29 May, 3.7% expected); core 3.1% (16 Jun). Standard fuel excise is back from 15 Jun; VAT 8% and price caps run to 30 June, with a VAT decision due 'shortly' (Tusk, 16 Jun).
policy.risk_text: A preliminary US-Iran deal (14-15 Jun) pushed Brent towards $80 and POLGB yields to three-month lows; risks: the MoU unravelling, the Fed dots (17 Jun), the fuel-package exit (excise back 15 Jun, VAT after 30 Jun) and two PLN 6-12bn sales; the 6.5-7% deficit keeps ASW wide.

macro.projection_text: NBP March projection (4 Mar; data to 19 Feb, war excluded): CPI 50% bands 1.6-2.9% (2026), 1.1-3.7% (2027); central path 2.3% / 2.4% / 2.3% (2026-28), GDP 3.9% in 2026; IMF (14 Apr): 2026 CPI 3.3%; EC (21 May): GDP 3.5% in 2026; OECD (June outlook): CPI 3.7% in 2026, no cuts before Q2 2027; Fitch (8 Jun): GDP 3.3%, NBP flat at 3.75% to year-end; World Bank (11 Jun): GDP 3.1% / 2.6%. The July projection is the next marker.
macro.fiscal_text: 2025 general-government deficit 7.3% of GDP (GUS EDP, 22 Apr), debt 59.7%; 2026 deficit cap PLN 271.7bn; budget deficit after May PLN 108.2bn (~40% of the limit, 15 Jun); the government's assumptions put the 2026 deficit at ~6.8% of GDP; EC (21 May): 6.5%, debt 64.5%; EKF consensus (2 Jun): 6.9%; EDP debt 61.6% of GDP at end-Q1 (10 Jun); 2027 budget path (9 Jun): GDP 3.1%, CPI 2.5%; the government adopted the windfall tax (16 Jun); fuel package (VAT 8%, price caps) to 30 June, standard excise back from 15 June.
macro.fiscal_risk_text: 2026 needs ~56% (MoF, 29 May) financed; budget accounts PLN 208.3bn at end-May (MoF, 8 Jun); 3 Jun switch (MoF database): PLN 11.63bn sold (demand 12.84bn) vs 10.90bn bought back (PS0527 7.42bn), net +0.73bn; OK0129 4.812%, PS0731 5.269%, DS0436 5.703%; BGK priced EUR 2bn of FPC bonds (2 Jun). S&P A-/stable (affirmed 8 May); Scope A negative (15 May); Fitch A- and Moody's A2 have negative outlooks; Fitch's June forecast round (8 Jun) was not a rating action.
macro.backdrop_text: The NBP held at 3.75% on 2 Jun; May CPI 3.1% y/y; Q1 GDP 3.5% y/y (second estimate). Ratings: Fitch A- negative, Moody's A2 negative, S&P A- stable. 16 Jun: May core CPI 3.1% y/y (-0.1% m/m; April 3.0%). Government adopted the windfall tax (~PLN 4bn for CPN). Tusk: fuel-VAT decision soon; Motyka: conditions to end price caps met (Brent ~$80). BGK: first FPC switch on 18 Jun (buys FPC0427). NBP FSR: the rising SPW share in bank balance sheets adds geopolitical sensitivity. NIK: MPC 2025 guidance gave limited information. PKO: SPW -5-10bp, 2Y/10Y at mid-April lows; DS0436 5.41%. Abroad: Brent fell below $80 (lowest since early March) as MS and GS cut forecasts; the BoJ hiked to 1.0% (7-1) and the RBA held at 4.35%. Bund 10Y 2.93% (nine-week low), HU10 5.14% (four-year low), UST10 4.44% with ~56% for a December Fed hike. ZEW jumped to +10.5; US housing starts hit a six-year low. The EP approved the EU-US tariff deal ahead of Trump's 4 July deadline; the CIA doubts Iran's nuclear concessions.

calendar.plan_text: MoF June plan (29 May): one switch on 3 Jun (settles 8 Jun; buys back DS0726, PS1026, WZ1126, OK0127, PS0527) and sale auctions on 17 and 24 Jun (PLN 6-12bn each) in OK0129, NZ0331, PS0731, DS0436 and NZ0936; no T-bills; ~56% of 2026 needs financed. 3 Jun switch (MoF database): PLN 11.63bn sold (demand 12.84bn) vs 10.90bn bought back (PS0527 7.42bn), net +0.73bn; OK0129 4.812%, PS0731 5.269%, DS0436 5.703%. BGK priced EUR 2bn of FPC bonds on 2 Jun; FPC switch on 18 Jun (buys back FPC0427).
calendar.timing_text: The Aug 2025-Feb 2026 pattern (auction-day close the cheapest point of the week) comes from a rally regime; March's sell-off broke it and April's auction days cheapened on average. Remaining June operations: 17 Jun, 24 Jun. Next MPC in July, with the NBP projection: a hold is expected.

facts.core_text: Regime: a preliminary US-Iran deal - Brent towards $80, core yields at two-month lows; the NBP held at 3.75% on 2 Jun while FRAs price roughly 15bp of NBP hikes; the ECB hiked to 2.25% on 11 Jun with one more hike priced, the Fed is priced for a 2026 hike, the BoE is priced for hikes, the CNB is on hold and the MNB is on hold. Poland's 5Y CDS was 50bp and the 10Y spread to Bunds 251bp on benchmark bonds (Erste, 16 Jun close). Brent below $80; BoJ hikes to 1.0% (16 Jun).

quasi_takeaways: FPC fixed lines trade ~{lo}-{hi}bp over the POLGB curve (average {avg}bp); widest ASW {widest} at {widest_asw}bp. Same State Treasury guarantee as POLGBs.
Best pickup: {best} ({best_sp}bp vs POLGB). For buy-and-hold books the guarantee makes the pickup attractive; liquidity is the cost (Pekao became BGK market maker on 13 Nov 2025).
Supply: BGK: Q3 issuance will mainly prefund the FPC's 2027 needs (~30% secured, 12 Jun); EUR 2bn priced on 2 Jun; FPC switch on 18 Jun (buys back FPC0427).
Use auctions, not Catalyst: trades are small retail lots and some lines go weeks without a print.
